english: Let $N=2^{6}\cdot3^{6}\cdot5^{4}\cdot7^{2}$. Then the number of ways of writing $N$ as a product $a\cdot b$ of two even positive integers $a$ and $b$, where $a\cdot b$ and $b\cdot a$ are regarded as the same, is ______.
hindi: माना कि $N=2^{6}\cdot3^{6}\cdot5^{4}\cdot7^{2}$ है। तब $N$ को दो सम धनात्मक पूर्णांकों $a$ तथा $b$ के गुणनफल $a\cdot b$ के रूप में लिखने के तरीकों की संख्या, जहाँ $a\cdot b$ तथा $b\cdot a$ को समान माना जाता है, ______ है।
solution: Unordered factorisations of a perfect square: $\dfrac{d(M)+1}{2}=\dfrac{526}{2}=263$
solution_full: If $a$ and $b$ are even with $ab=N$, write $a=2a'$, $b=2b'$. Then $a'b'=\dfrac{N}{4}=M=2^{4}\cdot3^{6}\cdot5^{4}\cdot7^{2}$, and conversely every factorisation $M=a'b'$ gives even $a=2a'$, $b=2b'$. So we count unordered factorisations of $M$.

Ordered factorisations $M=a'\cdot b'$ correspond to divisors $a'$: 525 of them. All exponents of $M$ are even, so $M$ is a perfect square with $\sqrt{M}=2^{2}\cdot3^{3}\cdot5^{2}\cdot7=18900$, and exactly one factorisation has $a'=b'$.
The other $524$ ordered factorisations pair off into $262$ unordered ones, so the number of unordered factorisations is $262+1=\dfrac{525+1}{2}=263$.
originality_note: New: factorisations of a perfect square into two factors under a parity restriction, which is removed by the substitution a = 2a', b = 2b' before the (d+1)/2 formula applies (way 5). Closest known: 'number of ways of writing N as a product of two factors' (d/2 or (d+1)/2). Different because: the restriction changes the number being factorised, and the student must check that N/4 is still a perfect square.
blueprint_concepts: Number of divisors, sum of divisors and product of divisors
Expressing N as a product of two factors (perfect square case)

concept_use.Number of divisors, sum of divisors and: d(M) = 5.7.5.3 = 525 is the number of divisors of N/4 from its prime factorisation.
concept_use.Expressing N as a product of two factors: N/4 is a perfect square, so its unordered factorisations number (d + 1)/2 = 263.
